proposals.protected_class: V3 lifecycle contract (root of trust; owner-only)
proposals.purpose: Add ONE recoverable lifecycle state, `technical_suspension`, with reasons RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED / SESSION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED / REVIEW_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED / REMEDIATION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED / HANDOFF_EVIDENCE_UNOBTAINABLE, so that an exhausted AUTOMATED retry budget is visible in the lifecycle instead of only in the ledger `suspensions` table. The reducer needs NO code change: it already handles any state declared under recoverable_states generically (entry from any non-terminal state, resume only to the recorded state, never a genuine blocker because it is not `blocked`).
proposals.verified: tests/d34-proposals.test.mjs applies the patch to a COPY of the lifecycle contract and drives the REAL reducer: entry from implementing, testing, independent_review, remediation and publishing; the only exit is the recorded resume target (remediation resumes to implementing); an owner_action_id is not required; it is not a blocked state; a wrong resume target and an unknown reason are refused. `git apply --check` is clean on the branch. NOT applied here: task-lifecycle.json is root of trust.
proposals.effects: changes the lifecycle contract digest the policy bootstrap pins; after the owner applies and re-pins it, `suspendTechnically` (orchestrator/suspension.mjs) gains one extra line — a reducer transition into technical_suspension with the same reason code — and the ledger `suspensions` row stays the scheduling source of truth. Until then the ledger-level suspension is the INACTIVE conservative solution and the reducer is untouched.
